lxc_43f710feb5973bcb.text: The reason is that luxury brands sell both an object and a meaning.

lxc_c525132c8c9b8240.text: A useful way to understand this is through four layers: object, story, access, and experience.

lxc_87b98bf0aa2431df.text: The object is the bag itself.

lxc_ff7c7c4ddbd9a6e3.text: The story connects it to a designer, place, or history.

lxc_6b2357fe0e81cf93.text: Access controls how easy it is to buy.

lxc_320cadbcbf23f768.text: Experience includes the shop, service, and packaging.

lxc_131ce61d4594ea76.text: Price sits around all four layers.

lxc_8d749e3d939a1ddb.text: In experiments with wine, people often judged the higher-priced wine more positively even when price was the main difference they knew.

lxc_2db50a7b9ed4fa40.text: A high price can therefore act as a price signal, although it does not prove quality by itself.

lxc_640deed792de341d.text: Together, these choices show how brands create a luxury feeling.

lxc_7e40518305231c9c.text: The object layer begins with materials, craftsmanship, and design.

lxc_045ec1f999fce09f.text: Craftsmanship means skilled work by trained makers.

lxc_ce73861df25c13bc.text: Hermès presents creation and craftsmanship as central parts of its strategy, and it runs training schools for leatherwork skills.

lxc_d6bbfaf92553fb5a.text: For a customer, careful stitching, smooth edges, balanced shapes, and strong parts can show time and attention.

lxc_5a32c0081b1c0650.text: However, luxury design does not always use large logos or bright decoration.

lxc_a036071bcb150a76.text: Some bags have one clean shape, one color, and only a small brand mark.

lxc_76fa1253759fbec2.text: This is often called quiet luxury.

lxc_80823155c34c98a9.text: The design seems confident because it does not shout for attention.

lxc_79ff56a79b42419c.text: A simple shape may also survive fashion changes better than a short trend.

lxc_877a09597cb3b3c7.text: The story layer gives an object a larger meaning.

lxc_6c9af66758f75d04.text: Louis Vuitton, for example, tells a history that begins with trunk-making and its first shop in Paris in 1854.

lxc_5bf76b518a2f1a2e.text: Its early flat-topped trunks answered a real travel problem because they were easier to stack.

lxc_ea97a2d048e86d1b.text: The company still describes its modern identity through that history of craft and innovation.

lxc_8aa7ac07edbbb67c.text: Stories like these link a modern bag to a place, a maker, and an earlier purpose.

lxc_1c1dcc0ddfe09ec4.text: They can also make an original product feel different from a copy.

lxc_77bc8370d608081d.text: A copy may have a similar shape, but it does not have the same official connection to the workshop, service, and documented history.

lxc_ba39b29034b9f90b.text: The access layer is about scarcity, which means that something is difficult to get.

lxc_ebd81b956dacfe7c.text: A brand may make a limited number, release one color for a short time, or give early access to selected customers.

lxc_95ee4cce1b876bab.text: Research on sustainable luxury products found that perceived scarcity could strengthen people's willingness to pay when they already liked a product.

lxc_18108f4b1c277292.text: The search can become part of the excitement.

lxc_6db5748bdfc32a75.text: A customer may wait, visit several shops, or feel proud after finding a rare design.

lxc_519eae279dc1458a.text: Hermès describes its own distribution network as exclusive, and says that each store chooses a different product selection.

lxc_3bdb072b95843287.text: Limited access can protect a special feeling, but it can also frustrate customers or make the brand seem controlling.

lxc_39951af09c8f4fb5.text: The experience layer begins before the customer touches the bag.

lxc_37c2f50e1d25088c.text: Luxury shops often use open space, careful lighting, quiet sound, and only a few products on display.

lxc_a4592229c0280160.text: Each bag receives attention instead of disappearing in a crowded shelf.

lxc_801ede8e31e20e1d.text: Hermès says its stores use unique architecture and different product selections to create a distinct experience, and it also trains sales teams.

lxc_9d41c70861679d0f.text: Personal service can add another layer: a salesperson may remember a customer's taste, arrange a private appointment, or help find a special color.

lxc_ca5fa44ba795a9d2.text: Finally, a strong box, soft dust bag, thick paper, and ribbon slow down the opening.

lxc_d94cf4133dcfbe38.text: The packaging protects the product, but it also turns an ordinary action into a small ceremony.

lxc_98cb6857db2af5a9.text: Luxury also has a social side.

lxc_10023d9246e7083a.text: A recognizable logo can tell other people about money, taste, or group membership.

lxc_e378f934e0155147.text: Researchers use the term brand prominence for how clearly a brand mark appears.

lxc_1eb3b5cc3bec517e.text: Their studies found that different customers preferred loud or quiet branding depending on the kind of status signal they wanted to send.

lxc_b26ac24712ec6695.text: This helps explain why one buyer wants a large logo while another chooses a design that only fashion fans recognize.

lxc_5a563109f890af3f.text: An actor, musician, or athlete can make the same bag seem elegant, creative, young, or powerful.

lxc_fe6c806722ad0677.text: The customer may not only think, “I like this bag.” They may also think, “This fits the person I want to be.”

lxc_acda7216c778cd08.text: The four layers must support one another.

lxc_5b30e93ce99f0279.text: A beautiful story cannot fully save a badly made bag, and excellent leather may not create luxury if the service feels careless.

lxc_01b9e51a199f9a1e.text: A high price can guide expectations, but the price experiments also show why buyers should look beyond the number.

lxc_1e65d28822f79415.text: Luxury can lose its power when quality falls, products become too common, staff treat customers poorly, or every design follows the same short trend.

lxc_1bb4f6a24f51e915.text: The strongest brands balance physical value and symbolic value.

lxc_70a919389603fda0.text: Physical value comes from the bag's material, design, and usefulness.

lxc_9628029f828f667f.text: Symbolic value comes from its story, rarity, experience, and social meaning.

lxc_a917331a11700631.text: The final question is personal: are those extra meanings valuable enough for the buyer?
